correctness.rationale: Condition on q and rotate the left Gaussian sketch into the orthonormal basis (q,q⊥). With row coefficients p=qᵀB, r=q⊥ᵀB the sketched response is Up+Vr with independent standard U,V. Conditional on U and q, the cross term has mean zero and UᵀV has variance W=||U||². The right Gaussian angle gives E q₁²=a/(a+b) (integrate via tan θ), so A=E||p||²=a²−ab+b² and D=E||r||²=ab. The conditional-on-U loss after averaging V and q is D+(Aλ²+DW)/(W+λ)². Its gap to the value at λ*=D/A is A W(λ−λ*)²/[(W+λ)²(W+λ*)], proving strict global optimality including the extended-risk endpoint λ=0. For zero ridge the squared loss is ||r||²(1+Z²/W) with independent normal Z and chi-square W; the density at zero yields the stated moment cutoff and E[1/W]=1/(s−2) when s>2. Positive ridge bounds √W/(W+λ), giving every positive error moment. For B=tI the mixed row term is traceless, so the trace shortfall is t(2−W/(W+λ)), strictly increasing from t. The isotropic beta tail follows from independent one- and s-degree chi-square terms.
residual_risks: The optimizer is for a deterministic ridge applied after QR normalization; a ridge chosen after observing q has a different, generally q-dependent optimum. No integrator or finite-precision claim was verified.

evidence: Dobriban–Wager cite the exact finite-sample Gaussian optimum γ_p/α² in their nλ ridge normalization, in addition to their high-dimensional theorem. For one feature and s samples with signal strength A/D, this gives sλ_D=D/A, exactly the frozen unscaled penalty.

Epperly–Webber's real-Gaussian unregularized conditional mean has the factor 1+1/(s−2) here. Nakatsukasa's generalized Nyström bound is for an unregularized estimator under its oversampling assumptions, and does not itself imply positive ridge tuning.
broader_coverage.reasoning: It is the exact finite-sample ridge identity, via equality of the conditional risk, that covers the positive optimum; neither an asymptotic ridge theorem nor an unregularized matrix error bound suffices by itself.
searches: arXiv:1507.03003, PDF pp. 3 and 31 (finite sample Bayes-optimal tuning)

evidence: The finite-sample ridge objective for fixed W has bias Aλ²/(W+λ)² and variance DW/(W+λ)², so the same optimizer works pointwise in W; the chi-square law supplies only the averaging distribution. A and D require only the right projection energy, not additional sketch-size-dependent analysis.

For identity B=tI the unregularized approximation has trace t, and multiplying it by W/(W+λ) strictly worsens its discrepancy from 2t. The positive-ridge moment restoration follows by bounding the same scalar filter.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new notation and precisely evaluated benchmark do not introduce a new mathematical step beyond projection, scalar ridge and the known unregularized distribution. The expected-value result is not obtained by averaging different conditional optimizers; it is obtained by the shared quadratic risk form after averaging the energies.

evidence: The QR-normalized pseudoinverse core is unregularized scalar-design sketch-and-solve for fixed q; replacement by (UᵀU+λ)⁻¹Uᵀ is exactly ordinary ridge.

After conditioning on U, selecting either response column with equal probability and multiplying its coefficient and noise by √2 turns vector-row risk into scalar coefficient risk. The resulting signal second moment is A and the noise covariance is D I, with zero signal–noise cross moment. Dividing response and coefficient by √D gives unit noise and signal second moment A/D.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Only the conditional second moments enter the squared coefficient risk of a linear ridge estimate. Independence between the actual signal and noise beyond the zero cross moment, or a Gaussian prior on p, is unnecessary: the Gaussian scalar surrogate gives the identical risk for every ridge. The full averaged problem is not the same as optimizing for each fixed q.

originality.rationale: The deterministic ridge is an exact specialization of the classical one-regressor bias–variance rule, not a new sketch-count independence mechanism. Condition on the normalized design U; the response is additive centered noise with second-moment trace D per left row and the coefficient has mean squared norm A independent of U. The standard scalar ridge risk and optimizer therefore apply at every U before averaging over its length. The ratio D/A uses the elementary two-dimensional Gaussian projection baseline. The indexed unregularized Gaussian reconstruction law already gives the tail mechanism, and on the identity the ridged approximation is the unregularized approximation multiplied by W/(W+λ), making the trace comparison immediate. No claim is made that a prior source prints the entire averaged formula in this notation.
residual_risks: No exhaustive priority claim and no assertion that an exact positive-ridge Nyström statement was found verbatim. The failing decision rests on the finite-sample risk equivalence and derivative-free minimizer identity, not inaccessible historical literature.

value.rationale: The benchmark clarifies that two losses need not agree and illustrates why QR normalization matters. In this rank-one isotropic-noise setting, however, the supposedly distinguishing exact penalty is the routine scalar ridge rule after inserting known or elementary projection energies, and the identity trace loss worsens by scalar shrinkage alone. The package does not establish a non-mechanical phenomenon beyond those textbook mechanisms.
residual_risks: This is not a judgment about the scientific value of general low-rank stage regularization or nontrivial loss tradeoffs in larger problems.
